> (there's still line formatting issue on Windows but I guess that's just Windows' problem...)

Is this only in the presence of Chinese characters?

When I try Chinese characters on my Windows 7 VM I just get question marks but I don't get incorrect formatting.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/536803/53481375-04f10600-3a75-11e9-8707-b9745c7e32e4.png)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/536803/53481444-2baf3c80-3a75-11e9-8983-8943255e9090.png)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/536803/53481483-3a95ef00-3a75-11e9-9923-3fd62128e153.png)

This is what it should have looked like

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/536803/53481724-b001bf80-3a75-11e9-92c3-d8d989e811e5.png)

Yes, the formatting issue occurs only in the presence of Chinese characters.
Supported codepage (e.g. cp936 aka GBK) and font (e.g. SimSun) are needed to display Chinese characters in Windows console.

I suspect the issue is due to some discrepancy (in Windows) between the width of a Chinese character when used in displaying the character and the width used to calculate length of a line. But it's not even consistent between different Windows consoles and codepages.

The formatting issue appears in my default `cmd` console (using the new rclone beta version):
![screenshot 2019-02-27 123405](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8552945/53510700-9a4bc480-3a8c-11e9-99b7-c29f4f7eb578.png)
Notice that, the width of a Chinese character is that of two English letters (which is pretty standard and looks well). After every line that has Chinese characters, the next line would be moved ahead a bit.

However, the line formatting appears to be correct in PowerShell:
![screenshot 2019-02-27 123408](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8552945/53510969-370e6200-3a8d-11e9-8acf-b1789c304b53.png)
Here, the width of a Chinese character is that of three English letters (which actually looks weird), and the lines are correctly formatted.

Line formatting is also correct in `cmd` console when I switch to UTF-8 codepage by `chcp 65001` (but then the font looks weird for some reason (unrelated to rclone)).
![screenshot 2019-02-27 124639](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8552945/53511166-c0259900-3a8d-11e9-9519-b255644c0890.png)
Again, the width of a Chinese character is that of three English letters.

On my Linux VM, width of a Chinese character is that of two English letters (which is good!) _and_ the line formatting is correct:
![screenshot 2019-02-27 125213](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8552945/53511684-f9123d80-3a8e-11e9-8d6a-262ca6d1e2fe.png)

So apparently, on Windows, when used to calculate the length of a line, every Chinese character counts as 3 cells, and formatting would be wrong if they're displayed using only 2 cells (which is actually the standard).

**Edit**: I should add that normally every Chinese character occupies 2 cells in all Windows consoles (cmd, PowerShell) under all supported codepages / encodings.
![screenshot 2019-02-27 143804](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8552945/53517730-5a410d80-3a9d-11e9-8cb9-d654d0bb7bdc.png)
![screenshot 2019-02-27 143949](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8552945/53517880-b4da6980-3a9d-11e9-9e8b-79ff5612c164.png)
![screenshot 2019-02-27 144033](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8552945/53517892-ba37b400-3a9d-11e9-8161-2a18cddf4639.png)

> So apparently, on Windows, when used to calculate the length of a line, every Chinese character counts as 3 cells, and formatting would be wrong if they're displayed using only 2 cells (which is actually the standard).

Can you compare the formatting in a cmd window for the release version and the beta version for me?

This problem is all about how wide the characters are displayed. Before all characters had a width of 1, but  I installed the [runewidth](https://github.com/mattn/go-runewidth) library to calculate it for the beta above.

Looking through the runewidth source code I find special handling for windows of the `936` code page under Windows.

https://github.com/mattn/go-runewidth/blob/master/runewidth_windows.go

Which lead me on to this

https://github.com/mattn/go-runewidth/blob/703b5e6b11ae25aeb2af9ebb5d5fdf8fa2575211/runewidth.go#L22-L32

So maybe setting the environment variable `RUNEWIDTH_EASTASIAN` to `0` or `1` might help - can you try that?

List of files in test folder:
```
0123456789ab
0一二三四
123456789xyz
上下左右
东南西北
四三二一
新建文件.txt
```

Release version, focus on the first line
![release-first](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8552945/53679011-d18cc200-3c94-11e9-8531-ed11cbfea615.png)

Release version, move focus to the last line
![release-last](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8552945/53679024-e701ec00-3c94-11e9-8283-f015a0221fa9.png)

Beta version, focus on the first line
![beta-first](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8552945/53679034-0e58b900-3c95-11e9-861e-9d38937d3776.png)

Beta version, focus on the last line
![beta-last](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8552945/53679039-17498a80-3c95-11e9-9b68-4290f4c5596d.png)

The results aren't deterministic. They could change depending on the entry point of `ncdu` command, or simply by chance.
Setting RUNEWIDTH_EASTASIAN to either 0 or 1 doesn't seem to have any effect in my system.

The simplest way to get Chinese (or more generally any CJK) characters displayed in CMD is to change CMD's font.
Open cmd.exe, and right click on the window title bar -> Properties -> Font, then you should find "SimSun" or "NSimSun" in the list, which is a Chinese font.

Another more complicated way (but more closely resembles a Chinese/CJK user's setup) is to change the system locale.
Go to Control Panel -> Region and Language -> (Region, if Win10) -> Administrative -> Change System Locale, and choose any one of the CJK locales. Then restart the computer, and CMD will be able to display CJK characters no matter which font it's using.

I just did some more testing and found one more complication.
It appears that `rclone ncdu` (both release and beta versions) formats lines with CJK characters correctly if Windows is under a CJK locale and CMD is using the "raster font". (Raster font cannot display CJK characters under non-CJK locale.)
![screenshot 2019-03-04 235409](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8552945/53781908-d6da4e80-3ed8-11e9-88c8-518291cbe999.png)
![screenshot 2019-03-04 235305](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/8552945/53781886-b4483580-3ed8-11e9-8705-fdc1191d7de6.png)
Line formatting is incorrect only if a TrueType font (i.e. most normal fonts) is used (which is the default).

I don't know what it means, but it smells like the issue is deep in the Windows rabbit hole.

Thank you for all your investigations.

I'll try to summarise.  I added some results I got from Windows 2016 server.

Before 997654d77decc569deb89927686a5ac8aab20ed0 Chinese characters which are wider than 1 ascii character were incorrectly displayed.

After that patch wide Chinese characters are correctly displayed in
- Linux termimals
- Windows powershell
    - OK on Windows 7
- Windows CMD prompt with
    - Any settings on Server 2016
    -  UTF-8 codepage by `chcp 65001` on Windows 7
    -  CJK locale and CMD is using the "raster font"

But they are incorrectly displayed in
- Windows CMD prompt with
    - TrueType font (i.e. most normal fonts) is used (which is the default) on Windows 7
- Powershell
    - Windows server 2016 - only displays every other character

> I don't know what it means, but it smells like the issue is deep in the Windows rabbit hole.

I'm inclined to agree with you! Powershell with Chinese characters on Win 2016 seemed to be broken.  If I type (cut and paste ;-) Chinese characters at the command prompt then attempt to edit them with the left and right cursor keys it corrupts the screen.

So what it looks like is that they fixed Windows 2016 CMD prompt but broke powershell.

Things are certainly working better than before.  I think to make them work perfectly involves working round bugs in various versions of Windows.  That would almost certainly have to be done in [termbox-go](https://github.com/nsf/termbox-go) or in [the runewidth library](https://github.com/mattn/go-runewidth) rather than rclone though.

Wow... the Windows Server 2016 results make things even more interesting now...

Given issues in the Windows console, I'm quite satisfied with rclone's current fix.
